chapter: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
title: Fate Marable and the riverboat calliope in the evenings
summary: As a child of six he heard Fate Marable on the Streckfus boats; he describes Marable as a quiet, light-complected, great reading pianist.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: What was it like as a kid, Danny, around here, other than that...?

Fantastic music. At six o'clock in the evening, you heard the calliope on the riverboat, in the summertime -- and in the wintertime. Then Fate Marable was out on the Marquis(?)... Fate Marable I can remember from like 1915, I'm six years old, in the evening. They didn't have all the noise that you have today, like automobiles and

trucks, and it was quiet, and you could hear that beautiful calliope on the river, Fate Marable was playing the latest melodies that the Streckfus people always made it their business to play... Like, "Twelfth Street Rag," you'd hear him playing that, or whatever, or playing "The St. Louis Blues." And he was the kingpin on he river, off of New Orleans to St. Paul, Minnesota. Fate Marable was the boss on the river. You'd hear musicians, White musicians, Black musicians, fellows(?) who hadn't played a while on the riverboat.
Fate Marable looked like Scoville Brown. That kind...
He would be a light-complected Black.
Didn't say much. Great piano player. Great full-handed piano player of that time. A reading musician. The Streckfus people had sent him out...
